## Summary

The agent gets a fourth scope, `multi_trace` (prose: "multi-trace standalone"). It analyzes two or more named jobs of one workload on one platform, for example the prefill and decode captures of one vLLM server, and writes a single report. Compute findings are ranked together, with every `impact_score` a percent of the combined GPU time of all jobs, and each P-item says which phase it came from. Kernel fusion and system analysis (CPU/idle, multi-kernel) run on one job the user picks, the `focus_job`.

**Includes a merge of #1126** (`0c9af963`, "Aggregate perf reports"). That merge brings `TraceLens/Reporting/aggregate_perf_reports.py` and the wrapper's `aggregation: {policy}` key, which write the combined `perf_report_aggregated_csvs/` with a `phase` column. The agent uses it unchanged. `a52ecebf` is that merge and also carries the feature; `9509e837`, `6ebc1f3b` and `c3e46e97` are prose and README follow-ups. To review the agent side only, diff `origin/staging_agent` against this branch over `TraceLens/Agent/`, `docs/how-to/agent.md`, `tests/test_analysis_agent_*.py` and `tests/test_reporting_utils.py`.

Single-trace and comparative runs are unchanged. Their CSVs have no `phase` column, so every phase lookup returns None and every new field is left out.

## Why

| Pain point | Old | New |
|---|---|---|
| One phase per report | A prefill and a decode capture needed two runs and two reports, with impact scores on different denominators | One run, one report. Every impact is a percent of the combined time, so P1 is the biggest win for the whole workload |
| Where a finding lives | n/a | Each compute P-item carries `**Phase**: <job>` and `phase=` on its marker; R6 validates it |
| Fusion and system analysis across jobs | n/a | Scoped to `focus_job`, with a scope line in the report. Fusion candidates come from one call tree, and idle time summed across separate captures is meaningless |
| Graph-replay-only, one trace | Step 0 aborted in Interactive mode; YAML mode already fell through to the Step 2 gate | Both modes continue to Step 2, which routes to the deterministic fallback. The `default`-mode "Trace Feature Detection" abort and its triage check are gone |
| Several "which CSV dir" maps | `perf_report_csv_dir` and `prepare_model_identification_data` each mapped scope to a directory | Prepare writes `focus_csv_dir` into the manifest; `perf_report_csv_dir` returns it and model identification calls it |

## Architecture

### End to end (`multi_trace` only)

```
run.yaml (or Step 0 answers)
  jobs: [{name: prefill, ...}, {name: decode, ...}]   one platform
  focus_job: decode
        │
        ▼
Step 0  config_utils check|build --scope multi_trace
          _shape_errors: 2+ jobs, one platform, phase == name
          check_config:  focus_job must name a job, then removed
                         jobs[i].phase := name
                         aggregation := {policy: combine_only_same_phase}
          variables:     trace_path / platform / capture_folder of the focus job,
                         comparison_scope=standalone, focus_job=decode
        │
        ▼
Step 1  TraceLens_generate_perf_report_from_config            (wrapper, #1126)
          perf_report_prefill_csvs/   perf_report_decode_csvs/
          perf_report_aggregated_csvs/   rows of every job, leading `phase` column,
                                         percentages over the combined time
          run_config.resolved.yaml
        │
        ▼
Step 2  check_graph_replay_coverage(aggregated unified_perf_summary.csv)
          graph-replay fraction per phase; the worst phase decides
          ── GRAPH_UNDER_RECORDED ─► deterministic fallback for the whole run
        │
        ▼
Steps 3-6  orchestrator_prepare --focus-job decode
          trace1_csv_dir = perf_report_aggregated_csvs/  ─► category CSVs (phase rides along)
          plan_reports(run_config.resolved.yaml) ─► per-job gpu_timeline.csv
                                                  ─► gpu_utilization.phases{prefill, decode}
          focus_csv_dir  = perf_report_decode_csvs/  ─► FusionCandidateBuilder
          Step 5 tree    = focus trace (+ focus capture merge)
          writes category_manifest.json:
            gpu_utilization       combined, plus .phases
            focus_job, focus_csv_dir, capture_folder (null when the merge fell back to raw)
          writes metadata/cpu_idle_metadata.json with the focus job's utilization
        │
        ├─────────────────────────────┐
        ▼                             ▼
Step 7  system (focus only)          Step 8  compute sub-agents (all phases)
  load_manifest_categories prints      build_operation_metrics ─► compute_impact_estimates
  phases[focus_job]; the CPU/Idle      ─► build_category_findings, grouped per phase
  and Multi-Kernel gates read it       ─► category_data/<cat>_metrics.json
  kernel_fusion_analysis stamps                          │
  phase = focus_job on its metrics                       │
        │                                                │
        └──────────────────┬─────────────────────────────┘
                           ▼
Step 8.5  generate_priority_data ─► priority_data.json   (one ranking across phases)
Step 12   analysis.md: Phase field and phase= on compute P-items, combined Total Time
          plus a per-phase sentence, "summed across phases" note on Top Operations,
          scope line on Fusion and System sections
          validate_report ─► _validate_report_priority_consistency:
            R6 marker phase == findings[N-1].phase
        │
        ▼
render_analysis_json(analysis.md)   (post-processing, run by the consumer)
  compute tasks bucket by (phase, operation) and carry task.phase
```

### Combined vs focus: who reads which numbers

```
category_manifest.json
  gpu_utilization.total_time_ms (combined) ──► compute impact denominators, Executive Summary Total Time
  gpu_utilization.phases[focus_job]       ──► load_manifest_categories (Step 7 gates),
                                              triage check_subagent_budget
  focus_csv_dir                           ──► perf_report_csv_dir ─► fusion, model identification
metadata/cpu_idle_metadata.json           ──► cpu-idle-analyzer (focus job)
metadata/<cat>_metadata.json              ──► compute analyzers (combined, unchanged)
```

### Fusion suppression stays in its phase

Fusion's high-confidence op keys suppress the matching compute rows so the same time is not claimed twice. Under `multi_trace` the same kernel and shapes can appear in both phases, so the key gains the phase:

```
kernel_fusion_metrics.json { phase: decode, high_confidence_op_keys: [...] }
        │  _load_fusion_op_keys ─► {(phase, *key)}
        ▼
build_operation_metrics: row matches only when (row.phase, *perf_row_key(...)) is in the set
        ─► decode rows suppressed, the identical prefill rows still scored
```

## What changed

### Python (10 files)

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `utils/config_utils.py` | `multi_trace` scope: shape errors (2+ jobs, one platform, `phase` equal to the name), `focus_job` check and removal, `phase` stamping, forced `aggregation` policy. The variables describe the focus job and add `focus_job` |
| `utils/orchestrator_prepare.py` | `--focus-job`: reads the aggregated CSVs, gets per-job utilization from the resolved config, builds fusion candidates from `focus_csv_dir`, and gives CPU/idle metadata the focus job's utilization. Manifest gains `focus_csv_dir`, `capture_folder`, `focus_job` and `gpu_utilization.phases`. Drops the unread `multi_kernel_metadata.json` |
| `category_analyses/analysis_utils.py` | `phase` carried from row to op metric, impact estimate and finding; findings grouped per phase; fusion keys matched per phase; `perf_report_csv_dir` returns the manifest's `focus_csv_dir` |
| `category_analyses/kernel_fusion_analysis.py` | Writes `phase` (the focus job) into `kernel_fusion_metrics.json` |
| `utils/report_utils.py` | `load_manifest_categories` prints the focus job's utilization; `prepare_model_identification_data` drops its `comparison_scope` argument and uses `perf_report_csv_dir` |
| `utils/deterministic_fallback.py` | Graph-replay coverage judged per phase; the reason names the worst phase |
| `utils/validation_utils.py` | R6: p_item marker `phase` must equal `findings[N-1].phase` |
| `post_processing/analysis_json.py` | Card marker attrs carry `phase`; compute tasks bucket by `(phase, operation)` and carry `phase`; phase breaks sort ties after operation |
| `post_processing/candidate_schema.py` | `ComputeTask.phase: NotRequired[str]` |
| `triage/checks.py` | `check_subagent_budget` reads the focus phase's idle percent; `check_gpu_graph_replay` (2h) removed with the prose that emitted its DIAG tag |

All paths are under `TraceLens/Agent/Analysis/`.

### Templates (2 files)

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `templates/analysis_template.md` | Rule 13 for multi-trace standalone. Executive Summary per-phase sentence, Top Operations "summed across phases" note, `**Phase**` line and `phase=` on compute P-items and their Detailed Analysis blocks, scope line on the Fusion and System sections |
| `templates/sub_agent_spec.md` | `**Phase**` line on P-item cards and reasoning candidates, `phase=` on the p_item marker, `phase` row in the `category_findings` field table |

### Sub-agent .md files (4)

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `agents/kernel-fusion-analyzer.md` | Candidates are the focus job's; no attribution to other phases |
| `agents/cpu-idle-analyzer.md` | Fallback reads `metadata/cpu_idle_metadata.json` (focus job on multi-trace) |
| `agents/multi-kernel-analyzer.md` | Inputs reduced to `multi_kernel_data.json`; dead missing-data branch removed |
| `agents/model-identification-agent.md` | `comparison_scope` input dropped |

### Orchestrator skill (2 files)

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `skills/analysis-orchestrator/reference.md` | Step 0 asks for **Scope** (four values, mapped to `<comparison_scope>`), with `multi_trace` branches for jobs, platform and capture folders; graph-replay-only continues to Step 2. Step 1 `--set focus_job`, Step 2 aggregated CSV path, prepare `--focus-job`, Step 7 gates on `phases[<focus_job>]`, Step 12 multi-trace lines, R6 remediation. "Trace Feature Detection" section removed |
| `skills/analysis-orchestrator/SKILL.md` | Index line drops "trace diagnostics" |

### Docs (2 files)

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `docs/how-to/agent.md` | `multi_trace` in the scope list and the scope table |
| `TraceLens/Agent/Analysis/README.md` | Multi-trace standalone mode, a Multi-trace column and graph-replay-only footnotes in Supported Analyses, a prompt example, `phase=` on the p_item marker |

### Tests (7 files)

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `tests/test_analysis_agent_config_utils.py` | `multi_trace` completion case and rejection params |
| `tests/test_analysis_agent_deterministic.py` | `test_detector_judges_each_phase` |
| `tests/test_analysis_agent_utils.py` | `test_findings_split_by_phase`, `test_priority_consistency_r6_phase_mismatch`, `test_build_operation_metrics_flags_only_the_fusion_phase`, `test_load_manifest_categories_prints_focus_job_utilization`; comparative model-identification test removed (covered by the manifest test) |
| `tests/test_analysis_agent_post_processing.py` | `test_compute_tasks_split_by_phase` |
| `tests/test_analysis_agent_triage.py` | `test_subagent_budget_gates_cpu_idle_on_focus_phase`; two graph-replay check tests removed |
| `tests/test_reporting_utils.py`, `tests/test_analysis_agent_category_utils.py` | `test_perf_report_csv_dir_reads_manifest` replaces the comparative-dir test; fixtures write `focus_csv_dir` |

## Known limitations

- **Joint ranking weights phases by capture length.** A long prefill capture can dominate the P-list. The Executive Summary's per-phase sentence shows each phase's window.
- **Triage, evals and Hyperloom find runs by `perf_report_csvs/`**, which a `multi_trace` run does not write, so they do not see these runs yet. The `analysis.json` change is additive (`phase` is optional), and Hyperloom's task loader does not read it.

## Test plan

- [x] `black` 26.3.1 clean on the 21 `.py` files in the diff; `lint-imports` 1 kept, 0 broken.
- [x] 1043 passed across the wrapper, config_utils, deterministic, utils, category_utils, post_processing, triage and reporting_utils test files (on `c3e46e97`).
- [x] Wrapper-only run on a prefill and decode capture: `phase` is exactly {prefill, decode}, `Percentage (%)` sums to 100, and the combined `gpu_timeline` total equals the sum of the two jobs.
- [x] `orchestrator_prepare --focus-job decode` on that output wrote `focus_job`, `focus_csv_dir` (ending `perf_report_decode_csvs`) and `gpu_utilization.phases`.
- [x] One agent run, from YAML, before the #1126 merge: one wrapper call, `focus_job=decode` printed, every compute p_item marker carried `phase=`, `validate_report` passed including R6, `analysis.json` compute tasks carried `phase`, and the fusion and system sections named decode. Not re-run after the merge or the switch from a `[<phase>]` heading tag to the `**Phase**` line.

## Net diff

```
Agent side:   27 files changed, 478 insertions(+), 207 deletions(-)
#1126 merge:   7 files changed, 522 insertions(+),  34 deletions(-)
Total:        34 files changed, 1000 insertions(+), 241 deletions(-)
```

+"""Combine the perf report CSVs of several traces into one report.
+
+Each input is a ``(phase, csv_dir)`` pair written by the perf report. Rows that
+share a table's row key are combined: times and counts add up, means and
+standard deviations are recomputed from the per-report counts, and min / max
+take the overall extreme. Percentages are recomputed from the combined totals,
+so they are shares of all reports together.
+
+Policies:
+
+* ``combine_only_same_phase`` — the phase is part of the row key. Reports of
+  the same phase combine; rows of different phases sit side by side.
+* ``combine`` — the phase is ignored and matching rows combine across all
+  reports. The ``phase`` column lists every contributing phase.
+
+``gpu_timeline`` is always one timeline summed over every report, so its
+``busy_time`` is the denominator for shares of the whole run.
+
+Medians and per-kernel summaries can't be combined exactly; they come from the
+contributing row with the most instances. A column or CSV without a rule
+raises ``AggregationError`` instead of being dropped.
+"""
+

+import os
+from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Sequence, Tuple

+import pandas as pd

+
+# Constants
+POLICY_SAME_PHASE = "combine_only_same_phase"
+POLICY_COMBINE = "combine"
+POLICIES = (POLICY_SAME_PHASE, POLICY_COMBINE)
+PHASE_COL = "phase"
+_PHASE_JOIN = "+"
+
+_GPU_TIMELINE = "gpu_timeline"
+_GPU_TIMELINE_TIME = "time ms"
+_GPU_TIMELINE_PCT = "percent"
+_GPU_TIMELINE_TOTAL = "total_time"
+_TABLE_KEYS = {
+    _GPU_TIMELINE: ("type",),
+    "ops_summary": ("name",),
+    "ops_summary_by_category": ("op category",),
+    "ops_unique_args": UNIQUE_ARGS_GROUPING_COLS,
+    "unified_perf_summary": UNIQUE_ARGS_GROUPING_COLS,
+}
+# Any other CSV with this column is a roofline sheet keyed by name and params.
+_ROOFLINE_MARKER = "name_count"
+_ROOFLINE_KEYS = ("name",)
+# Group-by columns a summary has only when it was grouped by them.
+_OPTIONAL_KEYS = (
+    "parent_module",
+    "overlapping_kernel_names",
+    "num_kernels",
+    "is_recompute",
+)
+# Instance counts that weight means and pool standard deviations.
+_COUNT_COLS = ("operation_count", "name_count")
+
+_SUM = "sum"
+_MEAN = "mean"
+_STD = "std"
+_MIN = "min"
+_MAX = "max"
+_FIRST = "first"
+_REPRESENTATIVE = "representative"
+_UNION = "union"
+_DERIVED = "derived"
+_NAMED_RULES = {
+    _GPU_TIMELINE_TIME: _SUM,
+    "operation_count": _SUM,
+    "name_count": _SUM,
+    "Count": _SUM,
+    "total_duration_us": _SUM,
+    "mean_duration_us": _MEAN,
+    "std_duration_us": _STD,
+    "ex_UID": _FIRST,
+    "GFLOPS": _FIRST,
+    "Data Moved (MB)": _FIRST,
+    "FLOPS/Byte": _FIRST,
+    "Compute Spec": _FIRST,
+    "Roofline Bound": _FIRST,
+    "perf_params": _FIRST,
+    "has_perf_model": _FIRST,
+    "entry_point": _FIRST,
+    "call_stack": _FIRST,
+    "call_stack_full": _FIRST,
+    "kernel_details_summary": _REPRESENTATIVE,
+    "kernel_details__summarize_kernel_stats": _REPRESENTATIVE,
+    "trunc_kernel_details": _REPRESENTATIVE,
+    "Categories": _UNION,
+    _GPU_TIMELINE_PCT: _DERIVED,
+    "Percentage (%)": _DERIVED,
+    "Cumulative Percentage (%)": _DERIVED,
+}
+_SUFFIX_RULES = (
+    ("_sum", _SUM),
+    ("_count", _SUM),
+    ("_ms", _SUM),
+    ("_mean", _MEAN),
+    ("_std", _STD),
+    ("_min", _MIN),
+    ("_max", _MAX),
+    ("_median", _REPRESENTATIVE),
+    ("_first", _FIRST),
+)

+_STD_TO_MEAN = {"std_duration_us": "mean_duration_us"}

+    "Kernel Time (µs)_sum",
+    "total_direct_kernel_time_sum",
+    "total_direct_kernel_time_ms",
+)

+_CUM_PCT_COL = "Cumulative Percentage (%)"
+
+
+class AggregationError(ValueError):
+    """The reports can't be combined: unknown input or invalid arguments."""
+
+
+def aggregate_perf_report_csvs(
+    reports: Sequence[Tuple[str, str]],
+    policy: str,
+    output_dir: Optional[str] = None,
+) -> Dict[str, pd.DataFrame]:
+    """Combine ``reports`` (``(phase, csv_dir)`` pairs) under ``policy``.
+
+    Returns one DataFrame per CSV name and writes them to ``output_dir`` when
+    it is given. Reports are read in order; ``first`` columns take the first
+    report that has the row.
+    """
+    if policy not in POLICIES:
+        raise AggregationError(
+            f"unknown aggregation policy {policy!r}; use one of: "
+            + ", ".join(POLICIES)
+            + "."
+        )
+    if not reports:
+        raise AggregationError("at least one report is required.")
+
+    tables: Dict[str, List[Tuple[str, pd.DataFrame]]] = {}
+    for phase, csv_dir in reports:
+        if not os.path.isdir(csv_dir):
+            raise AggregationError(f"report CSV directory not found: {csv_dir}")
+        for file_name in sorted(os.listdir(csv_dir)):
+            if not file_name.endswith(".csv"):
+                continue
+            table = file_name[: -len(".csv")]
+            df = _read_table(table, os.path.join(csv_dir, file_name))
+            tables.setdefault(table, []).append((phase, df))
+
+    result = {
+        table: _aggregate_table(table, frames, policy)
+        for table, frames in tables.items()
+    }
+    if output_dir is not None:
+        os.makedirs(output_dir, exist_ok=True)
+        for table, df in result.items():
+            df.to_csv(os.path.join(output_dir, f"{table}.csv"), index=False)
+    return result
+
+
+def _row_keys(table: str, columns: Sequence[str]) -> List[str]:
+    if table in _TABLE_KEYS:
+        base = list(_TABLE_KEYS[table])
+    elif _ROOFLINE_MARKER in columns:
+        base = list(_ROOFLINE_KEYS) + [
+            c for c in columns if c.startswith(PERF_PARAM_PREFIX)
+        ]
+    else:
+        raise AggregationError(
+            f"{table}.csv has no aggregation rule; add one to "
+            "TraceLens/Reporting/aggregate_perf_reports.py."
+        )
+    keys = [c for c in base if c in columns]
+    keys += [c for c in _OPTIONAL_KEYS if c in columns and c not in keys]
+    return keys
+
+
+def _column_rule(column: str) -> Optional[str]:
+    if column in _NAMED_RULES:
+        return _NAMED_RULES[column]
+    for suffix, rule in _SUFFIX_RULES:
+        if column.endswith(suffix):
+            return rule
+    return None
+
+
+def _read_table(table: str, path: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
+    # An aggregated report has a phase column; the caller's phase replaces it.
+    columns = [c for c in pd.read_csv(path, nrows=0).columns if c != PHASE_COL]
+    keys = _row_keys(table, columns)
+    unknown = [c for c in columns if c not in keys and _column_rule(c) is None]
+    if unknown:
+        raise AggregationError(
+            f"{table}.csv has columns without an aggregation rule: "
+            + ", ".join(unknown)
+            + "."
+        )
+    # Keys compare as text so 32 and 32.0 from different files don't split a row.
+    return pd.read_csv(path, dtype={k: str for k in keys})
+
+
+def _aggregate_table(
+    table: str, frames: List[Tuple[str, pd.DataFrame]], policy: str
+) -> pd.DataFrame:
+    tagged = []
+    for phase, df in frames:
+        df = df.drop(columns=[PHASE_COL], errors="ignore").copy()
+        df[PHASE_COL] = phase
+        tagged.append(df)
+    combined = pd.concat(tagged, ignore_index=True)
+    columns = [c for c in combined.columns if c != PHASE_COL]
+    keys = _row_keys(table, columns)
+    split_phases = policy == POLICY_SAME_PHASE and table != _GPU_TIMELINE
+    group_keys = keys + ([PHASE_COL] if split_phases else [])
+    count_col = next((c for c in _COUNT_COLS if c in columns), None)
+
+    rules = {c: _column_rule(c) for c in columns if c not in keys}
+    if count_col is None and any(r in (_MEAN, _STD) for r in rules.values()):
+        raise AggregationError(f"{table}.csv has means but no instance count column.")
+
+    rows = []
+    for _, positions in combined.groupby(
+        group_keys, dropna=False, sort=False
+    ).indices.items():
+        group = combined.iloc[positions]
+        row = {c: group[c].iloc[0] for c in keys}
+        row[PHASE_COL] = _PHASE_JOIN.join(sorted(set(group[PHASE_COL])))
+        weights = group[count_col].astype(float) if count_col else None
+        rep = (
+            group.loc[weights.idxmax()]
+            if weights is not None and weights.notna().any()
+            else group.iloc[0]
+        )
+        for col, rule in rules.items():
+            row[col] = _combine(col, rule, group, weights, rep)
+        rows.append(row)
+
+    out = pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=[PHASE_COL] + columns)
+    if table == _GPU_TIMELINE:
+        return _with_timeline_percent(out)
+    return _with_percentages(out)
+
+
+def _combine(col, rule, group, weights, rep):
+    values = group[col]
+    if rule == _SUM:
+        return pd.to_numeric(values).sum(min_count=1)
+    if rule == _FIRST:
+        present = values.dropna()
+        return present.iloc[0] if len(present) else np.nan
+    if rule == _REPRESENTATIVE:
+        return rep[col]
+    if rule == _MIN:
+        return pd.to_numeric(values).min()
+    if rule == _MAX:
+        return pd.to_numeric(values).max()
+    if rule == _UNION:
+        merged = set()
+        for value in values.dropna():
+            merged.update(ast.literal_eval(value))
+        return str(sorted(merged))
+    if rule == _MEAN:
+        return _weighted_mean(pd.to_numeric(values), weights)
+    if rule == _STD:
+        mean_col = _STD_TO_MEAN.get(col, col[: -len("_std")] + "_mean")
+        if mean_col not in group.columns:
+            raise AggregationError(f"{col} has no matching mean column {mean_col}.")
+        return _pooled_std(
+            pd.to_numeric(group[mean_col]), pd.to_numeric(values), weights
+        )
+    return np.nan

+
+def _weighted_mean(means: pd.Series, counts: pd.Series) -> float:
+    mask = means.notna() & counts.notna()
+    total = counts[mask].sum()
+    if total == 0:
+        return np.nan
+    return float((means[mask] * counts[mask]).sum() / total)
